subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Why is human oversight often recommended when AI systems make important decisions?
options: AI can make mistakes or reflect bias in its training data
Humans cannot understand any AI output
AI only works without electricity
AI always refuses to make any decision
questions.explain: AI can produce errors or biased outcomes, so human oversight helps catch and correct unfair or wrong decisions.

questions.q: A company stores its software and data on remote servers accessed over the internet instead of local machines. This is best described as:
options: Run-length encoding
Cloud computing
Virtual memory
An embedded system
questions.explain: Using remote internet-accessed servers for storage and software is cloud computing.

questions.q: What best describes machine learning?
options: A computer following a fixed set of rules written by a programmer
A method of compressing images without loss
A way of storing files on optical discs
Systems that improve their performance on a task by learning from data
questions.explain: Machine learning enables systems to improve at a task by finding patterns in data rather than being explicitly programmed with every rule.

questions.q: Which is a typical advantage of using robots for tasks such as deep-sea or bomb-disposal work?
options: They can operate in environments too dangerous for humans
They can replace the internet
They always feel fear and act cautiously
They never need any power source
questions.explain: Robots can work in hazardous environments, keeping human workers safe from danger.

questions.q: Which is a potential negative social impact of automation replacing manual jobs?
options: Lower running costs for businesses
Increased unemployment in some sectors
More consistent product quality
Faster production speeds
questions.explain: Automation can displace human workers, leading to job losses in some industries.

questions.q: Which technology allows devices to connect to a network without cables?
options: Wi-Fi
A USB cable
Fibre-optic cabling
Ethernet
questions.explain: Wi-Fi uses radio waves to connect devices to a network wirelessly.

questions.q: What is one reason a business might prefer cloud storage over buying its own servers?
options: It removes the need for any internet connection
It makes all data lossy
It can scale storage up or down without buying new hardware
Data is never stored anywhere
questions.explain: Cloud storage lets a business increase or decrease capacity on demand without purchasing and maintaining hardware.

questions.q: Which of the following is a drawback of cloud computing?
options: Backups are handled by the provider
It relies on a stable internet connection to access data
Storage can be increased easily
You can collaborate with others in real time
questions.explain: Cloud services depend on internet access, so you may be unable to reach your data if the connection fails.

questions.q: Which is a potential benefit of AI in healthcare?
options: Replacing the internet
Removing the need for any data security
Making patient records volatile
Helping detect patterns in medical scans to support diagnosis
questions.explain: AI can analyse medical images to spot patterns that support faster, more accurate diagnoses.

questions.q: Which is an example of an Internet of Things (IoT) device?
options: A smart thermostat that reports temperature and is controlled via an app
A printed paper map
A standalone calculator with no connectivity
A wired desktop keyboard
questions.explain: A smart thermostat collects data and connects to the internet, making it a classic IoT device.

questions.q: When you type a website address into a browser, which system translates the domain name into an IP address?
options: The operating system kernel
The DNS (Domain Name System)
The hard disk controller
The ALU
questions.explain: The DNS translates human-readable domain names into the numeric IP addresses computers use to locate servers.

questions.q: A self-driving car uses cameras and sensors to detect road signs and pedestrians. Which field does this mainly draw on?
options: Hexadecimal conversion
Artificial intelligence and machine learning
Magnetic storage
Lossless compression
questions.explain: Recognising objects from sensor data to make driving decisions is an application of AI and machine learning.

questions.q: On the web, what is the role of a web server?
options: It translates IP addresses into domain names exclusively
It only displays web pages on the user's screen
It stores website files and sends pages to browsers that request them
It physically connects two computers with a cable
questions.explain: A web server stores the files of a website and serves the requested pages back to the user's browser.

questions.q: What is a typical advantage of using robots in a car manufacturing factory?
options: They never require any maintenance
They can work continuously with high precision and consistency
They can show empathy to customers
They are always cheaper than humans in every situation
questions.explain: Robots can repeat tasks consistently and precisely for long periods without tiring.

questions.q: What is a common drawback of relying heavily on automated decision-making systems?
options: They make storage non-volatile
They never need any data
It can be hard to know how or why a decision was reached
They always run without electricity
questions.explain: Automated systems can be opaque, making it difficult to explain or challenge how a decision was made.

questions.q: Which statement comparing wired and wireless connections is correct?
options: Wireless connections are always faster than wired ones
Wired connections allow users to move freely around a building
Wireless connections never suffer from interference
Wired connections are generally more stable and faster; wireless offers greater mobility
questions.explain: Wired links are typically faster and more reliable, while wireless trades some speed and stability for mobility.

questions.q: What does IoT (Internet of Things) refer to?
options: A programming language for websites
Everyday objects with sensors and connectivity that exchange data over the internet
A method of compressing video files
A new type of CPU register
questions.explain: The IoT is the network of everyday devices fitted with sensors and internet connectivity that collect and share data.

questions.q: Which is a privacy concern raised by many IoT devices in the home?
options: They make the home network faster
They remove the need for passwords
They reduce electricity bills automatically
They may collect personal data that could be misused if not secured
questions.explain: IoT devices often gather personal data, which raises privacy and security risks if not properly protected.

questions.q: Which scenario best illustrates the IoT improving efficiency in agriculture?
options: Manually watering every field by hand
Storing crop records on an optical disc
Soil sensors automatically signalling irrigation systems when crops need water
A farmer reading a printed weather forecast
questions.explain: Networked sensors automatically triggering irrigation based on real-time data is an IoT application improving efficiency.

questions.q: What does it mean to train a machine learning model?
options: Showing it large amounts of data so it can learn patterns
Manually writing every rule the program will follow
Compressing the program to make it smaller
Converting the code into hexadecimal
questions.explain: Training a model means feeding it data so it can learn patterns and make predictions, rather than being explicitly programmed.

questions.q: Which is a realistic concern raised by the growth of artificial intelligence?
options: AI removing the need for any electricity
AI converting all files to hexadecimal
AI making all data storage volatile
Bias in decisions if the AI is trained on biased data
questions.explain: If AI is trained on biased data, it can make unfair or biased decisions, which is a significant ethical concern.

questions.q: Why can storing and processing data in large cloud data centres raise environmental concerns?
options: They remove the need for the internet
They consume large amounts of electricity for power and cooling
They make all data volatile
They convert files to lossy formats
questions.explain: Large data centres use significant electricity to run and cool their servers, which has an environmental impact.
